action.summary:
Triage of rows 11, 15, 33, 34 (Defender, Enterprise1, User3, User4) - observational assessment only. NOTE: The exact content of rows 11/15/33/34 and the prior-tick action history were not re-supplied in this prompt beyond the row identifiers, so specific IOCs cannot be cited verbatim; the assessment below is framed around the indicator-class patterns those rows typically carry in compromise telemetry (Defender AV events, Enterprise1 host telemetry, User3 account activity, User4 account activity) and explicitly flags this as an analytical limitation.

(a) Likely Threat Actor TTPs (MITRE ATT&CK mapping)
- Defender-side indicators (row 11) frequently capture defense-evasion / execution artifacts: AMSI/ETW tampering, PowerShell ScriptBlock logging bypass, suspicious signed-binary use (LOLBin abuse - T1218), or scheduled-task/service tampering (T1053.005). If the row reflects a single, low-prevalence, signed-binary child of an Office product, treat as transient scan noise; if it reflects tampering with AV itself, registry Run keys persistence (T1547.001), or service disable, treat as real persistence/evasion.
- Enterprise1 (row 15) - host endpoint indicator. Pattern-consistent with T1059 (scripting), T1003 (credential access / LSASS read), T1027 (obfuscated payload), or T1071 (C2). Real indicators typically show repeat occurrence, parent-child anomalies, or outbound to non-corporate ASN.
- User3 (row 33) - identity-side. Pattern-consistent with T1078 (valid accounts), T1098 (account manipulation), T1556 (MFA abuse), or inbox-rule persistence (T1564.008). Re-compromise-vs-noise hinge: rule creation on a previously-cleared mailbox, OAuth consent grants, or impossible-travel are real; a single sign-in from a new ASN that resolves to a managed device is more often noise.
- User4 (row 34) - identity-side. Same T1078 family considerations. If isolated, likely credential-stuffing noise; if correlated with row 33 (shared IP/ASN, similar UA, short window), treat as coordinated.

Without the literal payload of these rows I cannot confirm which specific TTPs apply; the above are the prior distributions for these indicator classes.

(b) Blast Radius
- Defender tamper: tenant-wide EDR blind spot - HIGH severity, worst-case blast radius is the entire Defender-managed estate for the duration the tamper survives.
- Enterprise1: scoped to that single host but may be a beachhead for lateral movement (T1021 RDP/SMB, T1570 lateral tooling) - MEDIUM, escalates to HIGH if LSASS-class indicators present.
- User3: scoped to User3's mailbox, OneDrive, OAuth-granted apps, and downstream collaborators. If the same user has been flagged on prior ticks, re-compromise expands blast radius to their team and any auto-forward recipients - MEDIUM-to-HIGH.
- User4: scoped to User4's access. If User4 is privileged (admin, finance, code-owner) blast radius is HIGH; if a low-privilege account it is LOW-MEDIUM. Risk compounds if row 33 and row 34 correlate (same actor, credential reuse).

(c) Recommended Containment Order (least to most disruptive, highest-confidence-first)
1. Enterprise1 (row 15) - network-isolate the host first; preserves volatile memory for IR while removing lateral-movement risk. Highest forensic value, lowest business disruption.
2. User3 (row 33) - if re-compromise confirmed via cross-tick correlation, suspend the account and revoke OAuth tokens + MFA factors before resetting password; this prevents session-hijack persistence. If no prior-tick correlation, step to a forced sign-out + token revocation only.
3. User4 (row 34) - conditional forced password reset + session revocation; do not disable until correlation with User3 is assessed.
4. Defender (row 11) - address last: collect tamper artifacts, then restore Defender service via known-good media. Removing AV protections early can mask further evidence and accelerate adversary TTPs; only after host containment and identity lockdown is it safe to repair EDR.

(d) Risk of Removing Now vs. Monitoring Another Step
- REMOVE NOW: justified only when an indicator independently meets a high-fidelity rule (AV tamper, LSASS read by unsigned process, OAuth consent grant to unverified publisher, impossible-travel + MFA fatigue). Removal before full correlation risks (i) tipping off an actor who has persistence elsewhere, (ii) destroying volatile evidence, (iii) business disruption on a false positive.
- MONITOR ONE MORE TICK: justified when the indicator is low-prevalence but not high-fidelity, when User3 vs. prior-tick correlation is the deciding question, or when removing would impair EDR coverage before host isolation.
- Default posture given uncertainty in this assessment: ISOLATE Enterprise1 NOW (lowest regret), CONDITIONALLY HARDEN User3 (revoke sessions, hold password reset pending one more tick of correlation data), MONITOR User4 one tick, DEFER Defender repair until step 2 unless the row clearly shows active tamper (not just a detection).

Uncertainty Statement
- High uncertainty: exact content of rows 11/15/33/34 not provided verbatim in this prompt, so TTP attributions and severity grades above are priors for these indicator classes, not observations.
- Medium uncertainty: whether User3 represents re-compromise versus a fresh but unrelated sign-in event - this is the single highest-value question for the next tick.
- Low uncertainty: general containment ordering principles (isolate hosts before identity actions before AV repair) hold regardless of which specific TTP is in evidence.

This report is final; no further role dispatches are available or permitted from the watcher role.
